conviction_note: Every direct counterparty that has spoken since Lam's 29 July call (TSMC, ASML, Samsung, Micron) points to a December-quarter step-up, and the stock has de-rated 24% in ten straight down sessions with no company-specific cause, so I lean long. But the December-quarter bar is single-sourced ($8.52B sell-side average against a published Morgan Stanley case for >$9B), so the buy-side hurdle is probably above the printed consensus, and 25-delta skew pays modestly for downside (+3.0 vol pts). p_up 57 on an 8% absolute move gives +1.1. That is about half the +2.0 sum of the findings, because the findings are proxies and positioning, not a Lam number.
bar: September quarter (FQ1'27): company guide revenue $8.1B +/- $0.4B, non-GAAP GM 52% +/- 1, op margin 39.5% +/- 1, EPS $2.15 +/- $0.15 (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/lam-research-q1-2027-earnings-preview-lrcx-results-preview, 2026-10-05). Consensus is $8.13B / $2.18 from two agreeing sources: Hudson Labs, and Seeking Alpha's Morgan Stanley note via https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:93c889d67094b:0-morgan-stanley-expects-lam-research-to-guide-9b-plus-for-december-quarter/. The December-quarter guide is the line the stock trades on. Its bar is single-sourced: the Yahoo average is $8.52B revenue / $2.31 EPS with a high of $9B, while Morgan Stanley writes it 'would not rule out' a guide above $9B. On the WebSearch summary of https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/LRCX/analysis/ that is snippet_only, so every guidance finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 2.3% of float, down from 2.5% in early September (Benzinga sentiment snapshot of 2026-09-25, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LRCX/sentiment). The last full settlement I found was 32.9M shares, 2.94% of float, 3.55 days to cover, as of 2026-05-15 (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/LRCX/short-interest). That is not crowded and gives no squeeze mechanism. Baseline: 25-delta skew +3.04 vol pts (modest put premium), put/call OI 0.63, event implied move 6.63% (straddle 7.11%). Run-up is -12.8% over 20 days and -6.6% over 5 days, and spot is 38% below the 30 June high of $433.33. Ten straight down sessions to $263.94 on 2026-10-16 (-24%, the longest streak since the 1984 listing), with sell-side ratings still 21 of 22 Buy.

findings.finding: Customers and peers that spoke after Lam's 29 July call all point to a December-quarter equipment step-up, which supports a December guide above the $8.52B sell-side average. TSMC (15 Oct) kept 2026 capex at $60-64B after spending $13.8B in Q3, so Q4 needs $19.4-23.4B (+40-70% q/q), and it said 2026-28 capex will be 'significantly higher'. ASML (14 Oct) guided Q4 sales to EUR 14.2-15.2B from EUR 11.7B in Q3 and said 2027-28 supply will not meet demand. Samsung's Q3 operating profit was a record KRW 107.4T, with memory around KRW 110T. Micron (30 Sep) raised capex, with first-half FY27 near $25B. The market expects a December guide of about $8.5B (sell-side), against a Morgan Stanley case for more than $9B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the line Lam trades on. On 2026-07-29 a September guide about 14% above consensus ($8.1B vs ~$7.11B) bought +17.98% close to close (baseline; https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/07/30/lam-research-soars-after-record-results-and-strong-outlook/). Five of the last seven prints were up, with a median absolute move of 4.45%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the stock had priced the counterparties' acceleration it would not have fallen 24% in ten sessions straight through TSMC's and ASML's prints; equipment lagged the chipmakers' rebound on 20 Oct. The published December consensus of $8.52B is only about +5% q/q, below what TSMC's implied Q4 capex step and Morgan Stanley's >$9B case suggest. Against that, sell-side previews (MS, UBS 'even more robust guidance') are public, so part of this is the whisper, and the finding is a customer proxy, not Lam's own number.
findings.independence: Several independent counterparties. ASML Q4 guide and supply commentary: https://investinglive.com/stocks/asml-says-2027-and-2028-supply-will-fall-short-of-demand-as-q3-sales-hit-a-record/ (2026-10-14). Samsung Q3 preliminary: https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-earnings-guidance-for-third-quarter-2026 (2026-10-08). Micron capex: https://www.mobileworldlive.com/ai-cloud/micron-ramps-capex-to-address-shortage/ (Sep 2026). Morgan Stanley expects the WFE run-rate above $200B (+60% y/y) in the December quarter (tradingview link in bar).

findings.finding: The December-quarter bar is higher than the printed consensus. The sell-side average is $8.52B (high $9B), while Morgan Stanley (Oct 5, PT $385) says it would not rule out a guide above $9B, citing DRAM and 2nm pull-ins, and UBS expects 'even more robust guidance'. A guide in the $8.6-8.9B band would 'beat consensus' and could still disappoint the buy-side number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-04-22 Lam fell 2.63% after its print. The baseline does not say on which line; I found no source tying that fall to the guide, so I record only the move.
findings.why_not_priced: The sell-side average in data feeds ($8.52B) is not the number holders will judge the guide against. If the higher bar were fully reflected in the $8.52B, Yahoo's high and average would be close together. The 24% drawdown partly lowers this whisper, which is why the finding is small.
findings.independence: UBS 'very strong report and even more robust guidance', via https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/lam-research-stock-falls-nine-straight-sessions-down-21-7/53639693 (2026-10-16). It shares the MS note with finding 1's bar context: two readings of one bar, but opposite in effect (finding 1 is the fundamental, this is the hurdle).

findings.finding: Positioning was washed out into the print with no company-specific cause. Lam had ten straight down sessions to $263.94 on 16 Oct (-24%, about $104B of market value, the longest losing streak since its 1984 listing). The trigger was Applied Materials declining to give a WFE forecast at its 13 Oct investor day, plus profit-taking. Equipment names kept lagging chipmakers on 20 Oct, and spot is $267.89, 38% below the June high, on about 34x forward earnings.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July print came after a 10% one-day drop on 2 July on 'AI capex peak' fears, with the stock at $252 into the print, and it rallied +17.98%. That is one prior case of a washed-out setup followed by a strong guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is itself the price. The question is whether the reaction to a good guide is asymmetric. Skew is only +3 vol pts, so the option market is not pricing a skewed downside after a 24% fall. If holders were still crowded long, I would expect a steeper put skew and the stock holding up with chips on 20 Oct, and it did not.
findings.independence: Applied Materials investor-day trigger: https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/2675610673. Equipment lagging chips on 20 Oct: https://www.aol.com/articles/chip-stocks-shrug-off-scary-154222000.html (2026-10-20). Profit-taking with fundamentals intact: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/19/lam-research-imploded-by-20-in-the-last-3-months-this-respected-wall-street-firm-says-its-about-to-double/ (2026-10-19).

findings.finding: The September quarter is likely at or above the guide midpoint: consensus is $8.13B / $2.18 against a $8.1B +/- $0.4B / $2.15 guide, and Lam has beaten EPS five quarters in a row. This lands inside what the company already guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: June quarter: revenue $6.72B and record EPS $1.82 beat. The reaction was driven by the guide, not the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Consensus sits on the guide midpoint, so a beat toward the top of the range is the usual pattern and small.

findings.finding: China is the open risk to the December guide and to the commentary. China fell to 26% of revenue in the June quarter from 34%. The BIS Affiliates (50%) rule suspension was due to lapse on 10 Nov 2026; Bessent extended the trade truce to 10 Jan 2027 (23 Sep), but whether the Affiliates rule stays suspended is reported as unresolved.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In the July print China dropped from 34% to 26% of revenue and the stock still rose 18%, so a falling China mix has been absorbed when the rest grows.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced and known. What is not known is how management frames China in the December guide around a rule whose status is unresolved; a cautious China comment would pull the guide toward the sell-side number. Netted against the rest of the company: non-China (memory, leading-edge logic) is about 74% of revenue and accelerating per finding 1, so the net size is small.
findings.independence: Affiliates rule unresolved: https://www.bkl.co.kr/en/law/insight/newsletter/6811. China mix 34% to 26%: Hudson Labs preview (finding 4's source).

outside_window.finding: BIS Affiliates rule suspension nominally lapses on 10 Nov 2026 unless extended; the trade truce runs to 10 Jan 2027. A re-imposition would hit Lam's China revenue.
SK hynix (about 23 Oct KST) and ASM International (27 Oct) report after the exit window; their capex and order commentary cannot reach this trade.

baseline_tension: A long lean cuts against the modest put skew (+3.0 vol pts) and goes with buying a 24% drawdown. The case for the option market being too cautious is that the drawdown had no Lam-specific cause, and every counterparty since July (TSMC, ASML, Samsung, Micron) printed or guided up. The case against is that ASML's ADR fell on a strong quarter, so 'good is priced' is a live pattern in this group this month; that keeps p_up at 57, not higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): the December-quarter bar rests on one estimate source plus a broker's opinion, so the counterparty guidance finding is capped from +2.0 to +1.5.
Rule 7 (positioning): the long positioning finding goes against a positive put skew, so it moves from +1.5 to +1.0, and p_up moves from 58 to 57.

Rule 5 (proxy): TSMC, ASML, Samsung and Micron are direct customers or peers, not macro, so finding 1 stays filed with independence marked as a counterparty proxy. The drawdown has a named cause and LRCX is not a microcap, so the positioning finding is not zeroed.
Rule 1 (reaction function): Lam has bought its guide raises (+18% in July, 5 of 7 prints up), so there is no veto. The reported-quarter finding stays near zero because it lands inside the guide.
Rule 9 (net of the rest): the China finding is sized net of the roughly 74% non-China revenue and left at -0.3.
